question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dupleix — Headquarters and territories of French India]
options: Pondicherry (Puducherry) — Main headquarters of French India where Dupleix was based as Governor-General
Chandernagore — French trading post in Bengal that Dupleix governed before becoming Governor-General
Masulipatnam — French trading post on the Coromandel coast under French influence during Dupleix's time
Surat — Primary headquarters of French East India Company (Compagnie des Indes) in Western India under Dupleix's direct command
wrong_fact: Surat was NOT the primary headquarters of the French East India Company under Dupleix. Surat was primarily a Dutch and English trading centre. The French headquarters was Pondicherry (Puducherry) on the Coromandel coast. The French also had Chandernagore in Bengal, but Surat was never under Dupleix's direct command as headquarters.
explanation: Joseph François Dupleix served as the Governor-General of French India (1742–1754) with his headquarters at Pondicherry (Puducherry). He had previously governed the French settlement of Chandernagore in Bengal. The French had trading posts at Pondicherry, Chandernagore, Mahe, Karikal, and Yanam — not at Surat. Surat was historically dominated by the English and Dutch East India Companies.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dupleix — Carnatic Wars and associated battles/places]
options: Siege of Pondicherry (1748) — British Admiral Boscawen failed to capture Pondicherry during the First Carnatic War
Trichinopoly (Tiruchirappalli) — Became a key contested city in the Second Carnatic War between French and British-backed candidates
Arcot — Robert Clive's famous capture of Arcot (1751) was a turning point that weakened French strategic position in the Carnatic
Wandiwash (Vandavasi) — Dupleix personally led French forces to victory here in 1760, decisively defeating the British
wrong_fact: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) was NOT a French victory and Dupleix did NOT lead forces there. Dupleix was recalled to France in 1754. Wandiwash was won by the BRITISH (under Sir Eyre Coote) against the French (under Lally), six years after Dupleix had left India.
explanation: Dupleix was recalled to France in 1754 after the failure of French policy in the Carnatic. The decisive Battle of Wandiwash (22 January 1760) took place six years after his recall — the British under Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French under Count de Lally. This effectively ended French political ambitions in India. The Siege of Pondicherry (1748), Trichinopoly's contested position, and Robert Clive's Arcot campaign (1751) all occurred during Dupleix's tenure and are correctly matched.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Dupleix — Political alliances and geographic spheres of influence]
options: Muzaffar Jung — Dupleix supported him as Nizam of Hyderabad; French influence was extended to the Deccan
Chanda Sahib — Dupleix backed him as Nawab of the Carnatic; French candidate opposed by the British
Tanjore (Thanjavur) — French under Dupleix captured and annexed Tanjore as a permanent French territory in South India
Hyderabad — Dupleix's alliance with Muzaffar Jung (Nizam) gave French control over vast territories in the Deccan
wrong_fact: Tanjore was NOT captured and annexed by the French as a permanent territory. Dupleix's sphere of influence was in the Carnatic (backing Chanda Sahib) and the Deccan (backing Muzaffar Jung as Nizam), but Tanjore remained under its Maratha rulers and was never a French possession.
explanation: Dupleix's political strategy involved backing Indian claimants: Chanda Sahib for the Nawabship of the Carnatic and Muzaffar Jung for the Nizamate of Hyderabad. In return, the French received territories and revenues. After Muzaffar Jung's death (1751), his successor Salabat Jung (backed by French officer Bussy) gave French influence in the Deccan (including the Northern Sarkars). However, Tanjore (Thanjavur) was never a French territorial acquisition — it remained under its Maratha dynasty throughout this period.
